theme: Let Me See Who I Must Face
hindi: अर्जुन कहते हैं: जब तक मैं युद्ध की इच्छा से खड़े इन योद्धाओं को अच्छी तरह देख न लूँ, तब तक रथ वहीं रोके रखिए। मुझे जानना है कि इस युद्ध के प्रयास में मुझे किन-किन के साथ लड़ना है।
english: Arjuna says to Krishna, “Stop the chariot until I have looked carefully at these warriors standing ready and eager to fight. I want to see exactly who I must fight in this great battle.”
deeper: Arjuna is not running away yet. He is doing something wise: he wants to see clearly before he acts. A good archer first looks at the field, the distance and the wind. Arjuna wants to look at the whole situation with open eyes.

Notice the words yoddhu-kāmān, “eager to fight.” Arjuna sees people who are ready and burning with energy. Looking carefully at what is in front of us is the first step to understanding it. But looking can also bring up feelings we did not expect, and that is exactly what happens in the next verses.

The verse teaches a gentle lesson. Before any big task, such as an exam, a match or a hard talk with a friend, pause and look at what you are really facing. A calm, honest look helps us choose well. Later in the Gita, Krishna will help Arjuna see even more clearly.
words: I look carefully at, I observe
those who are eager to fight
in this effort or undertaking of battle
background: The two great armies, the Pandavas and the Kauravas, stood face to face at Kurukshetra. The Pandava conches had just sounded, and their thundering call shook the hearts of Dhritarashtra’s sons (1.19). The fighting was about to begin.

Arjuna lifted his bow and looked at the Kaurava army standing in battle order (1.20). Then he asked Krishna, who was his charioteer, to place the chariot between the two armies (1.21). In this verse, he explains why: he wants to see who is standing there to fight.
lessons: Taking a calm look at a situation helps us act wisely.
Stopping for a moment is not weakness; it gives us time to think.
It is easier to handle a challenge when we understand it clearly.
Arjuna turns to Krishna, and we too can ask a wise elder or friend to guide us.
When we look closely at something big, our feelings can surprise us, and that is okay.
examples: Diya reaches the exam hall early and reads the whole question paper first. She sees which questions are easy and which need more time. Then she begins calmly.
Before the cricket match, Aryan walks around the ground. He notices the dry patch and the short boundary. Now he knows how to plan his game.
Meena stops at the edge of the busy road and looks left and right. Only when she sees clearly does she cross. A careful look keeps her safe.
Before the school play, Kabir peeps through the curtain to see the audience. At first his tummy flutters. But seeing familiar faces makes him ready for his turn.
Sana opens a big jigsaw puzzle. Before touching any piece, she studies the picture on the box. Understanding the whole makes the work easier.
Rohan is upset with Imran. Before saying angry words, he stops and thinks about what really happened. This helps him speak kindly.
Before jumping in, Tara checks how deep the pool is and where the steps are. She then jumps in with confidence, not just courage.
Nandini is unsure which club to join at school. She sits with her grandmother and talks it through. Seeing things with a wise person’s help makes her choice clear.

story.title: Ishaan and the Chess Tournament Board
paras: Ishaan was ten years old and had come to his first inter-school chess tournament in Pune. His hands were cold with nerves. Teams were already sitting at the long tables, and the clocks were ticking.

His coach, Mrs. Kulkarni, said, “Ishaan, before you sit, let us look at the board and the list. Let us see whom you will play today.” Ishaan took a deep breath and read the names slowly. He had been trying not to look, because looking made it feel real.

As he read, his worry started to shrink. His first opponent was a girl from another school who liked the same opening moves he had practised. He even smiled when he saw a boy from his own neighbourhood on the list. Knowing what was ahead made him feel steady.

Ishaan sat down, shook hands with his opponent and began his game. He did not win every round that day, but he played each one with a clear mind. On the bus home, he told his coach, “It was easier once I actually looked.”
story.moral: Lesson: A calm, honest look at what lies ahead helps us face it with a clear mind.

quiz.q: What does Arjuna ask for in this verse?
o: To look carefully at those standing ready to fight
quiz.x: He wants to observe the warriors he would have to face.

o: Those who are eager to fight
quiz.x: Yoddhu-kāma means one who wishes to fight.
Arjuna is speaking to Krishna, his charioteer.

quiz.q: What everyday lesson can we take from this verse?
o: Look at a situation clearly before you act
quiz.x: Pausing to see clearly helps us make wise choices.

reel.hook: Why did Arjuna stop the chariot before the battle began?
reel.lesson: Pause and look clearly at what you face before you act.
reel.caption:
Before the big moment, Arjuna paused to look and understand. 👀
Try it today: take one calm look before you begin your task.
What will you look at carefully today? 🙏
